instantiated_cells.justification: Clients (principals) must file semi-annual reports due July 15 and January 15, not annual reports.
The statute requires clients to file semi-annual reports, not monthly reports.
Client periodic spending disclosure is specified as a semi-annual report with set due dates, with no alternative 'other' frequency provided.
The statute sets semi-annual filing dates for clients and does not provide for quarterly filing.
Clients meeting the threshold must file 'semi-annual reports' by July 15 and January 15.
The statute requires semi-annual reporting on fixed dates and does not tie client reporting to a tri-annual legislative calendar.

The semi-annual report content lists client identifying info, lobbyists, subjects, and expenses/compensation but does not require disclosure of whether the client’s business is public or private or its nature of business.
The client report must include 'the compensation paid or owed to each such lobbyist' which is direct lobbying compensation cost.
Clients must report 'the name of the person, organization, or legislative body before which such client has lobbied,' which discloses contact targets.
The report must include 'a description of the general subject or subjects' lobbied.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: NY Legis L § 1-J(b)(5)(i)-(ii) (2015); NY Legis L § 1-C(j) (2015)
instantiated_cells.justification: Clients must report 'any other expenses paid or incurred... for the purpose of lobbying' and the statute defines 'gift' broadly as a thing of value, making such non-compensation costs reportable when incurred for lobbying.
Beyond lobbyist compensation, the client must disclose 'any other expenses paid or incurred... for the purpose of lobbying,' i.e., indirect/non-compensation costs.
The semi-annual report must include each retained lobbyist’s 'name, address and telephone number.'
Clients must list 'each lobbyist retained, employed or designated' by the client.
Qualifying clients that spend over $50,000 and meet the 3% threshold must report sources of funding over $5,000 used to fund lobbying activities.
The report must include 'the name, address and telephone number of the client.'
Clients must report 'the legislative bill numbers of any bills' lobbied.
The client must disclose both lobbyist compensation and 'any other expenses paid or incurred' for lobbying, covering total lobbying expenditures reported by the principal.
The client’s semi-annual report must include 'the compensation paid or owed to each such lobbyist,' requiring disclosure of salary/fees paid.
Expenses over $75 must be 'detailed as to amount, to whom paid, and for what purpose,' which is itemization rather than only lump-sum reporting.
The statute specifies report contents but does not require associations/representative groups to list all sponsors or members.

The client report requires listing each lobbyist retained/employed/designated, but does not specifically require listing individual lobbyists employed by a lobbying firm/company beyond those representing the client.
